name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen90
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After change_1m_bps beyond ±5, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After change_5m_bps beyond ±15, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The larger the recent move, the stronger the pull back toward consolidation.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

CRITICAL PRINCIPLE: CALIBRATE HALF_WIDTH TO ACTUAL VOLATILITY, NOT YOUR GUESS

The feedback shows the pattern clearly:
- Tight spreads (1.0-2.0 bps) on volatile conditions destroy skill
- When you quote ±1.5 bps after a 5-minute move of 10+ bps, you get run over
- When you quote ±2.4 bps after a 20 bps rise, the market moves 6.7 bps and you miss by 10.3 bps (skill -0.54)
- When you quote ±3.8 bps after a 40 bps rise with 60 minutes to funding, the market moves 24.5 bps and you miss by 18.7 bps (skill +0.24 but still hit on both sides)

The scoring harshly penalizes being outside your spread. Missing by 8-10 bps turns positive skill negative.

Default spread calibration by recent realized volatility:

NARROW spreads (half_width 1.5-2.5 bps) ONLY when ALL of:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 5.0
- taker_buy_share between 0.40 and 0.60
- trades < 600 for BTC, < 500 for ETH, < 300 for SOL
- not 0-2 UTC, not 13-15 UTC, not within 60 min of funding
- looking back 10 minutes in the candlesticks, no bar moved more than 3 bps

MODERATE spreads (half_width 4.0-5.5 bps) when:
- |change_1m_bps| in 2-6 range, OR |change_5m_bps| in 6-15 range
- OR taker_buy_share in 0.30-0.40 or 0.60-0.70 (modest imbalance)
- OR 60-120 minutes from funding
- OR modest volume (600-1500 trades for BTC, 500-1200 for ETH, 300-800 for SOL in the last bar)

WIDE spreads (half_width 6.5-9.0 bps) when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 6
- |change_5m_bps| > 15
- taker_buy_share > 0.75 or < 0.25 in the last bar
- within 60 minutes of funding
- during 13:30-14:30 UTC
- high volume bar (>2000 trades for BTC, >2500 for ETH, >1000 for SOL)

VERY WIDE spreads (half_width 10.0-15.0 bps) when:
- |change_5m_bps| > 30 (extended move, high reversion risk but uncertain magnitude)
- |change_1m_bps| > 10 combined with extreme tape
- Within 15 minutes of funding after a large move
- Multiple conflicting signals (e.g., heavy buying but price falling, or extreme imbalance that just reversed)

The examples show the cost of under-sizing half_width:
- Example 2: change_5m +7.9 bps, quoted ±3.9 bps, actual -9.8 bps → should have quoted ±7 bps
- Example 3: change_5m +19.9 bps, quoted ±2.4 bps, actual +6.7 bps → should have quoted ±8 bps minimum
- Example 6: change_5m -18.0 bps, quoted ±2.6 bps, actual +5.2 bps → should have quoted ±8 bps
- Example 7: change_5m +39.7 bps, 60 min to funding, quoted ±3.8 bps, actual -24.5 bps → should have quoted ±12 bps

Correct calibration:
- Example 1: change_5m +6.6 bps, quoted ±4.0 bps, actual +1.8 bps → good sizing, skill -0.99 but only because the move was small
- Example 8: change_5m -0.5 bps, low volume (532 trades), quoted ±1.5 bps, actual -1.0 bps → correctly sized for quiet conditions, skill +0.29

Direction selection after volatility:
- Default to mean reversion when |change_5m_bps| > 12 and no persistent driver
- Reduce |delta_bps| magnitude when uncertain—quote 0 bps ±8 bps rather than -5 bps ±3 bps after conflicting signals
- After a large 5-minute move, expect at least a partial snapback: if change_5m is +20 bps, forecast -3 to -6 bps
- Check if the 5-minute move was steady (all bars same direction) or a spike (one or two big bars): spikes revert faster and harder

When volume and tape conflict with price:
- Heavy buying (>0.7) but price flat or down: quote wide (±7-9 bps), neutral to slight up bias
- Heavy selling (<0.3) but price flat or up: quote wide (±7-9 bps), neutral to slight down bias
- Low volume (<300 trades for BTC) makes every signal noisier: add 2-3 bps to half_width

Funding proximity overrides other signals:
- Within 15 minutes of funding: half_width minimum 8 bps, no matter how quiet the tape looks
- 15-60 minutes from funding: half_width minimum 5 bps
- After a large move (>20 bps in 5 minutes) within 60 minutes of funding: half_width minimum 10 bps

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. When facing large recent moves or conflicting signals, widen half_width_bps rather than pretend you know the direction. The scoring penalizes being outside your quoted range far more than it rewards tight correct quotes.

Better to quote ±9 bps and capture the move inside your range than quote ±3 bps and miss by 10 bps, even if the wide quote looks "imprecise."

The target is not to predict the exact move—it is to quote a range that captures the realized move while still being tradeable. After change_5m of 15+ bps, you should almost never quote a half_width under 6 bps.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
